thread:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — loader refactor: we need to decide behavior when a shard read returns partial data. Two options on table: 1) strict: block application until shard fully verified, 2) permissive: return a 'repairable' partial buffer and let async repair fill gaps. Thoughts?
aj: I favor permissive for p99 latency, but only if we can guarantee no silent corruption. We need an explicit validity bitmap + a light checksum per chunk.
maria: Exactly. My sketch: operator returns a handle object plus a blob-level validity bitmap and a status enum {OK, REPAIR_PENDING, CORRUPTED}. The runtime must treat CORRUPTED as fatal; REPAIR_PENDING allows computation to continue if model annotation permits.
sylvia: For checksums I'd push adler32 by default — cheaper than crc32 and more than nothing. We should allow a stronger checksum opt-in. Chunk size should be aligned to storage block size (e.g. 64 KiB) so partial transfers match object store behavior.
leo: Important callout: quantized blocks and some fused ops are fragile. For those models we should prefer strict. Add a manifest flag at model-level: "partial_policy": "deny" | "allow_tolerant" | "allow_strict".
jordan: Ops + infra concerns: repair storms if many replicas try to repair the same missing chunk. We should elect a single repair leader per shard (etcd/consul lease or local token bucket) and have exponential backoff plus jitter for fallback repairers. Also track a per-shard repair_rps limit.
aj: We also need to prevent memory accounting gaps: partial buffers count fully against GPU memory reservation to avoid OOM surprises. If we zero-fill missing chunks to reduce jitter we must still mark validity.
maria: Agreed. Implementation notes: handle is a thin indirection to buffer; expose handle.await_repair(timeout_ms) and handle.validity_bitmap() so callers can decide. If repair completes in-place we keep the same buffer; otherwise we swap and emit a short event: "repair.swap" with old/new pointers for tracing.
sylvia: Manifest proposal snippet (in thread):
```json
{
  "format": "redwood-shard-manifest-v1",
  "chunk_size": 65536,
  "chunk_checksums": ["adler32", "..."],
  "partial_policy": "allow_tolerant",
  "annotations": { "model_sensitive": false }
}
```
leo: If manifest absent, runtime should default to strict behavior unless the deployment config sets global allow_partial_missing_manifest=true. We must document compatibility: older safetensors bundles without sidecar manifest => strict-by-default.
jordan: Telemetry/metrics: emit repair.requests, repair.leader_acquired, repair.success, repair.failed, repair.swap_count. Also emit per-model histograms for repair latency.
aj: Tests: we need a simulated harness that flips partial reads mid-transfer and verifies both strict and permissive flows. Also simulate leader loss and ensure fallback repairs with backoff.
maria: Deployment note: canary the loader-refactor with permissive=false first, then run permissive on small percentage. deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: 2026-04-03T02:00Z -> us-west-2 (per infra calendar).

sylvia: Action items: 1) I will draft the manifest schema doc and conversion guide for existing safetensors bundles; 2) I will add handle API docs and example usage showing await_repair; 3) jordan and aj, can you sketch leader election backoff pseudocode?
jordan: I can. Will post pseudocode and token-bucket sketch.

leo: I'll own the test harness + CI scenarios. Plan: unit tests for bitmap semantics and integration test that runs a toy model with zero-fill vs block modes.
maria: Great. If nobody objects I'll land the operator shim and wire config defaults to strict by default, manifest opt-in for permissive. We'll iterate after canary. Ping here if any red flags. :thumbsup:
